name: Tower width & proportion (CDDG)
question: Is the tower narrow and slender enough to read as a tower rather than a slab under Vancouver's City-wide Design and Development Guidelines?
method: Reads each tower's plan sides and height from Layer 0. Compares the wider plan side with the CDDG tower dimension guideline (29.0 m, or clear articulation), the height-to-width ratio with the CDDG proportion tip (6:1 to 8:1 or more), and the wider side as a share of the site frontage with the CDDG slab tip (roughly 60%). Shows plate area with no threshold until the CDDG floorplate maxima by use are extracted.
human: Whether the tower shows clear volumetric articulation (S2.3.2 accepts a wider tower that does), how it reads on the skyline and from the street, and the City's own urban design review.
limits: Rectangular towers from Tower Design Toolkit's massing only: no setbacks, tapers or articulation. Ignores rotation when comparing with the frontage. The CDDG text is the draft in the 15 Jul 2026 Council report (approved 28 Jul, effective 27 Oct 2026): check the final guideline. Tips are guidance, not rules, so this node never fails a tower on them; it says Check.

parameters.label: Site frontage the tower faces
parameters.note: The long side of the competition block. In Real Vancouver, set it to your own site's frontage.

metrics.label: Widest tower plan dimension

threshold.text: at most 29.0 m, or clear volumetric articulation

source.label: City of Vancouver, Council Report RTS 18459, Appendix A: draft City-wide Design and Development Guidelines (CDDG)
source.page: S2.3.2 tower dimension, mixed-use and non-residential contexts (text read in research packet P06, rounds 1–2)

metrics.note: Above 29.0 m the guideline asks for clear volumetric articulation, which this node can't see, so it says Check rather than Fail.

metrics.label: Height-to-width ratio

threshold.text: 6:1 to 8:1 or more reads proportionate (a tip, not a rule)

source.label: City of Vancouver, draft CDDG design tip on tower proportions, as summarised in research packet P06
source.page: Clause number not recorded; wording taken from the packet's parameter notes, not re-read

metrics.note: Uses the wider plan side, so a slab reads less slender than a square tower of the same area.

metrics.label: Tower width as a share of the frontage

threshold.text: below roughly 60% of the frontage; wider towers often read as slabs (a tip)

source.label: City of Vancouver, draft CDDG design tip on tower width and frontage, as summarised in research packet P06
source.page: Clause number not recorded; wording taken from the packet's parameter notes, not re-read

source.label: City of Vancouver, draft CDDG average floorplate maxima by use (named in research packet P06)

falseAssumptions.claim: The 18.3 m Downtown podium height (S2.2.7) applies to every tower.
falseAssumptions.correction: S2.2.7 applies only to exclusively residential towers ('residential development' in the CDDG glossary). Mixed-use and non-residential tower podiums follow Table 2.2b (S2.2.6), which steps with street width: up to 15.2 m (streets up to 27.5 m wide), 15.2–18.3 m (up to 30.5 m) and 18.3–23.0 m (wider).

source.label: City of Vancouver, Council Report RTS 18459, Appendix A: draft CDDG
source.page: Glossary; S2.2.6, S2.2.7, Table 2.2b (corrected in research packet P06, rounds 1–2)

brief.name: Tower width & proportion (CDDG)
brief.function: Compares each tower's widest plan side with the CDDG 29 m guideline, its height-to-width ratio with the 6:1 tip and its width with the site frontage; shows plate area for information. Says Check, never Fail, on tips.
brief.notes: Show the tower's width, e.g. a dimension along its base. No check mark or warning sign: the node compares with guidance and says Check, never Fail, on tips.
